$comment: Hand-maintained decisions the TypeScript declarations cannot express.
`number`: every field derived from a TS `number`, mapped to "int" or "float".
TS has one numeric type, neither .d.ts uses `bigint`, and no JSDoc tag encodes
the distinction, so nothing in the input carries the answer.
Exhaustive both ways: a `number` field with no entry fails the run, and so does
an entry matching no emitted field -- neither a field added upstream nor a
Keys are "Model.field": the FINAL emitted model name with the ORIGINAL camelCase
field name, singularized for array aliases -- `LeaderboardEntry.globalRank`, not
"int" for counts, ranks, sizes, channels and millisecond timestamps; "float"
when the value can legitimately be fractional. When you cannot tell, choose
float: a wrong "int" truncates real data silently on the Variant->int assignment
in from_dict() (a 92.47s lap time becomes 92), while a wrong "float" only reads
less nicely. That asymmetry is also why there are no name heuristics (*Count,
*Rank, max*) -- their false positives land on the unsafe side.
